description.narrative:
In 2020-2021, two institutions - Federation of Professional Trade Associations in Ghana (FEPTAG) and Hospitality Coaching Consult embed SCORE Training as part of their business development service portfolio to improve productivity and working conditions in Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the Trading and Hospitality sectors. In October 2020, the Gender Equality module was introduced to improve opportunities and working conditions at the workplace for women.
The number of certified trainers available are 29 with 26% being females. Six of these are Expert Trainers of whom 1 is a female. As at July 2021, about 230 enterprises have received SCORE training to improve their productivity, quality and competitiveness. About 17% of these enterprises are female owned. Besides, 2,081 staff of diffreent enterprises have been trained; 34% are females. National training of trainers (including certification) and quality assurance systems are in place to enable trainers deliver training consistent with the standards of the ILO. Score Training Solutions Ghana (STSG) and Management Development and Productivity Institute (MDPI) are currently in charge of these systems. ILO with funding from the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (NORAD) has provided the relevant Technical Assistance and guidance throughout the implementation of the SCORE programme. The framework for the delivery of the training, the training materials including manuals, PPT slides/ notes, videos etc were developed and the Training of Trainers conducted with the assistance of the ILO. In June 2021, the ILO also facilitated the establishment of a quality assurance system to guide the implementation and ensure that training meets international standards.
The ILO coordinated the activities of the National Tripartite Advisory Committee (NTAC), which is the coordinating body for SCORE. Four NTAC meetings were held from January 2020 to march 2021. NTAC is made up of representatives from Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations (MELR), Ghana Employers' Association (GEA), Ghana Trades Union Congress (GTUC), State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), Norwegian Agency for Development Corporation (NORAD) Ministry of Tourism, Department of Labour, Management Development and Productivity Institute (MDPI), Department of Factory Inspectors, and Industrial and Commercial Workers Union (ICU).

description.narrative: In November 2020, the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations validated the National Green Jobs Strategy, as a response to the provisions made in the National Employment Policy on green jobs. After consultations with multi-stakeholder ecosystem actors, including the social partners, who were organised in working groups to develop action plans and priority entry areas, the National Green Jobs Strategy was developed to provide a framework for the promotion of Green Jobs in Ghana. The National Green Jobs Strategy was developed to create platforms, develop capacities and institute measures that would organise and harmonise on-going green interventions through effective coordination. The strategy adopted a multi-sectoral approach to ensure effective delivery of goods and services by specialised state and non-state actors through the implementation of measures that support the growth and expansion of the green economy in Ghana - Supporting Green Enterprises for Decent Job Creations (2021-2025). The Strategy was launched in March 2021. With support from Sweden through the SIDA-ILO Partnership, ILO provided technical support to the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations and the tripartite partners to develop the National Green Jobs Strategy. The ILO facilitated the initial stakeholder workshop in January 2020 and reinforced the capacity of the tripartite constituents to develop a Green Jobs Policy Analysis Document through consultations with other relevant stakeholders. The ILO reviewed the National Green Jobs Strategy and supported its validation workshop in November 2020.
